note: Lean propagates Cauchy-ness one level at a time through a step that is a contraction on the same unmarked representation. It does not use [M]'s metric with the bound 2, the halving, or the discrepancy delta_i(N,N') between two cutoffs.

lemma winds (m:ℕ) (h:r≤ m): CauchySeq (fun n=> y' m n) :=by
     have h' (i:ℕ)(h:r ≤ i): ∀ᶠ n in atTop,y' i n=(T' i h n|>.leanings (W (i+1) n)) (y' (i+1) n):=(L'.sails.eventually (eventually_gt_atTop i)).mono fun n hn=> ((B' n).tallies hG b hz hc hR ht (V n) (hV n) i h hn).2 _
     apply (Matric.Gear.spends (cheerful hG b hz hc hR ht B' L' hZ V hV) _ h' m h)
     have hh:Tendsto (fun _ : ℕ=> y) atTop (𝓝 y):= tendsto_const_nhds
     apply Tendsto.cauchySeq (x:=y) (hh.congr' ?_); filter_upwards [L'.sails.eventually (eventually_ge_atTop r)] with n hn; exact ((he n hn).reads _ |>.trans ((V n).terminal.apply_symm_apply _))|>.symm

proof_context.conclusion: `winds` proves the Cauchy property at level `m` by feeding the base case and the relation `p' i n = leaning (p' (i+1) n)` between consecutive levels into `Matric.Gear.spends`.

snippet.text:
lemma spends {p':∀ m:ℕ,ℕ →F.Coeff}(ht:CauchySeq (p' k))(he:∀ i:ℕ,∀ h:k ≤ i ,∀ᶠ n in atTop,p' i n=(T i h n|>.leanings (W (i+1) n)) (p' (i+1) n))(v:ℕ)(hv:k≤v): CauchySeq (p' v):=by
     induction v,hv using Nat.le_induction with
     | base=>exact ht
     | succ v h ih=>
       apply succor (Ritzy.invests (Q.tight v h) (Q.voyages (v+1) (by omega))) (zero_lt_one.trans_le (Q.tight v h).senior) (fun i x=> (T v h i).hail (W (v+1) i) _) ih (he v h) -- Iiff orientation

proof_context.conclusion: `spends` propagates the Cauchy property down one level at a time by `Nat.le_induction` with the contraction data `Q.tight`.
